disposition.title: Kajitani's cyclic arboricity conjecture for matroids
disposition.literal_statement:
Let $M$ be a finite loopless matroid with ground set $E$ and rank function $r(A)$ for subsets $A\subseteq E$. A **cyclic ordering** of $E$ is an ordering considered cyclically, and a block of $r(M)$ cyclically consecutive elements is a base when it has rank $r(M)$. **Kajitani's conjecture.** There is a cyclic ordering of $E$ such that every $r(M)$ cyclically consecutive elements are bases of $M$ if and only if, for every non-empty subset $A\subseteq E$, 
$$
\frac{|A|}{r(A)}\leq\frac{|E|}{r(M)}.
$$
 This conjecture is a much more general formulation of the preceding cyclic-ordering questions; the source reports no resolution, while noting that the two-base generalisation has no known results for $k\geq3$.

disposition.title: The blow-up conjecture for globally rigid graph constructions
disposition.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph with $v>1$ vertices, denoted $v_1,\ldots,v_v$. Replacing each vertex $v_i$ by an independent set of size $a_i$ and connecting the new independent sets according to the edges of $G$ gives a graph constructed from $G$ by independent-set blow-ups.

**Blow-up conjecture.** For any connected graph $G$ with $v > 1$, there exists some $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_v$ and some $d$ such that if we replace each $v_i$ with an independent set of size $a_i$ and connect them accordingly, the resulting graph is GPR in $\mathbb{R}^d$.

This conjecture proposes a globally rigid construction for every connected graph with more than one vertex, extending the paper's experimentally observed and proved examples for irreducible graphs of small order, $k$-chains, and $k$-rings. The general assertion remains open in the supplied text.
disposition.source_name: Samuel Frank and Jiayang Jiang, “New Classes of Counterexamples to Hendrickson's Global Rigidity Conjecture”, arXiv:0909.2893 (2010).
disposition.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0909.2893

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2009).

disposition.title: Lemke–Kleitman conjecture on indices of sequences over cyclic groups
disposition.statement:
Let $Z_n$ be the cyclic group of $n$ elements, let $d$ and $n$ be positive integers with $d\mid n$, and let $S$ be a sequence of $n$ elements in $Z_n$. For a subsequence $T$ of $S$, write $\sigma(|mT|_n)$ for the sum of the least positive representatives of the terms of $mT$, where $m$ is coprime to $n$. **Lemke–Kleitman conjecture.** There should exist a nonempty subsequence $T$ of $S$ and an integer $m$ coprime to $n$ such that

$$
d\mid\sigma(|mT|_n)\mid n.
$$

The case $d=n$ asserts that every sequence of $n$ elements in $Z_n$ contains a subsequence of index $n$. The paper states that this conjecture is false in general, giving counterexamples for $n=4k+2\geq22$, although related assertions hold under repetition hypotheses and are believed in some prime-order cases.
disposition.source_name: Weidong Gao, Yuanlin Li, Jiangtao Peng, Chris Plyley and Guoqing Wang, “On the Index of Sequences over Cyclic Groups”, arXiv:0909.2461 (2011).
disposition.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0909.2461

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of September 2009); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

disposition.title: Freeness conjecture for the sharp transform of the planar binary tree algebra
disposition.statement:
Let ${\bf PBT}$ be the Loday–Ronco algebra of planar binary trees, and let ${\bf PBT}^\sharp$ denote its $\sharp$-transform. For each tree $T$ with at least two nodes and empty right subtree at the root, let ${\bf P}_T^\sharp$ be the corresponding sharp-transformed element.

**Freeness conjecture.** The algebra ${\bf PBT}^\sharp$ is free over the set ${\bf P}_T^\sharp$, where $T$ runs over trees with at least two nodes and such that the right subtree of the root is empty.

The claim describes a proposed free generating set for the sharp-transformed planar binary tree algebra. The supplied text gives no evidence that this assertion has been resolved.

disposition.title: Pomerance conjecture on four-term minimal zero-sum sequences
disposition.statement:
Let $Z_n$ be the cyclic group of $n$ elements. A sequence is **minimal zero-sum** if its sum is zero in $Z_n$ and no proper nonempty subsequence has sum zero. Its index is

$$
\operatorname{Index}(S)=\min_{(m,n)=1}\{\sigma(|mS|_n)\}.
$$

**Pomerance conjecture.** If $n$ is a positive integer with $(n,6)=1$ and $S$ is a minimal zero-sum sequence in $Z_n$ with $|S|=4$, then

$$
\operatorname{Index}(S)=n.
$$

Results cited in the paper establish the analogous assertion for minimal zero-sum sequences of length at most three and of length at least $n/2+1$, while the four-term case under the stated coprimality condition is presented as conjectural.
disposition.source_name: Weidong Gao, Yuanlin Li, Jiangtao Peng, Chris Plyley and Guoqing Wang, “On the Index of Sequences over Cyclic Groups”, arXiv:0909.2461 (2011).
disposition.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0909.2461

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2009).

disposition.title: Universality of the polymatroid quasi-symmetric invariant
disposition.statement:
Let $\operatorname{PolyMat}$ be the vector space of polymatroids, let $\operatorname{QSym}$ be the quasi-symmetric-function space, and let ${\mathcal G}:\operatorname{PolyMat}\to\operatorname{QSym}$ be the valuative invariant in the preceding theorem. A map $f:\operatorname{PolyMat}\to V$ is **valuative** when it preserves every rational linear relation among polymatroid base polytopes. **Universality conjecture.** For every $\mathbb{Q}$-linear valuative map $f:\operatorname{PolyMat}\to V$, there should exist a $\mathbb{Q}$-linear map $\psi:\operatorname{QSym}\to V$ such that

$$
\psi\circ {\mathcal G}=f.
$$

This asks whether every valuative invariant factors through ${\mathcal G}$; the supplied text does not establish whether this universal property holds.
disposition.source_name: Harm Derksen, “Symmetric and Quasi-Symmetric Functions associated to Polymatroids”, arXiv:0801.4393 (2008).
disposition.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0801.4393
